compactMembership.notes: Colorado's electrician reciprocity operates via NERA (National Electrical Reciprocal Alliance) bylaws — a voluntary multi-state reciprocity ARRANGEMENT that still requires applying for and being issued a separate Colorado license, NOT a single multistate license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact, e.g. the Nurse Licensure Compact). Recorded as false to avoid conflating NERA with a compact under this field's actual schema meaning.

reciprocityRules.value: Colorado follows National Electrical Reciprocal Alliance (NERA) bylaws for the Journeyman Electrician license. A journeyman or master electrician certificate from a qualifying state may be reciprocated to a Colorado journeyman license without a written examination, provided the certificate is current/active/in good standing, was obtained by a state-administered examination (not by grandfathering without an exam), and has been held for at least 1 year. Qualifying states (14): Alaska, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Utah, Wyoming.

requiredExperience.notes: Colorado's ORIGINAL (non-reciprocal) journeyman licensure requires 8,000 hours / 4 years of supervised experience plus 288 classroom hours — but that figure describes the standard path for someone with NO prior out-of-state license, not the reciprocity eligibility condition itself, and was sourced only via a secondary source (contractorlicenserequirements.com) in Phase 2D.1, not independently confirmed against an official page. Not recorded as this field's value to avoid conflating the two distinct pathways.
